day_title: Day 01: Automated Missing Value Imputation (KNN vs MICE)
chapter_title: Automated Missing Value Imputation (KNN vs MICE)
prerequisites: MCAR vs MAR vs MNAR Mechanisms

critical_concepts.concept: Missing Data Taxonomy (MCAR vs MAR vs MNAR)
critical_concepts.definition: Classifying missingness into Missing Completely at Random, Missing at Random, or Missing Not at Random.
critical_concepts.elaboration: Agents analyze feature correlation matrices to determine if missing values depend on observed variables (MAR, suitable for MICE/KNN) or unobserved biases (MNAR, requiring explicit missingness indicator flags).
critical_concepts.industry_application: Prevents catastrophic downstream model bias caused by naive mean/median imputation on correlated datasets.

critical_concepts.definition: Iteratively modeling each feature with missing values as a function of all other features in a chained regression cycle.
critical_concepts.elaboration: Agents preserve feature covariance and variance distributions without collapsing data toward artificial central tendencies.
critical_concepts.industry_application: Standard gold-standard preprocessing step for clinical, financial, and credit risk modeling.

theory_content.title: Autonomous Missing Value Imputation & Variance Preservation
theory_content.content: Blindly dropping rows with missing values shrinks training datasets and introduces severe selection bias. An Agentic Data Preprocessing Specialist implements statistical tests to classify missingness mechanisms and deploy multivariate imputation strategies.
theory_content.practical_takeaway: Never use mean imputation on skewed or high-variance distributions; use KNN or MICE.
theory_content.analogy: Like restoring a missing piece of a torn historical painting by analyzing the colors and brush strokes of all surrounding areas rather than slapping a patch of grey paint over the hole.
theory_content.industry_case_study: In a clinical sepsis prediction study, naive mean imputation underestimated patient mortality risk by 18% because severely ill patients had more frequent missing lab tests due to transfer delays. Switching to MICE restored predictive accuracy.

interactive_questions.title: Select Imputation Strategy for Correlated Medical Clinical Dataset
interactive_questions.prompt: In a hospital patient dataset (10,000 records), 'Serum Creatinine' is missing in 8% of rows. Creatinine is strongly correlated with 'Patient Age' (r=0.62) and 'Blood Urea Nitrogen' (r=0.78).
interactive_questions.question: What imputation strategy should the autonomous preprocessing agent execute?
options: Delete all rows containing any missing Creatinine values
Apply MICE (Multivariate Imputation by Chained Equations) using Age and BUN as predictive covariates, and add a binary missingness indicator column `creatinine_was_missing`
Fill all missing Creatinine values with 0.0
Replace all missing values with the maximum observed Creatinine value
interactive_questions.answer: Apply MICE (Multivariate Imputation by Chained Equations) using Age and BUN as predictive covariates, and add a binary missingness indicator column `creatinine_was_missing`
interactive_questions.explanation: Because Creatinine is strongly correlated with Age and BUN (Missing at Random), MICE accurately predicts missing values using the joint distribution. The missingness indicator captures any residual diagnostic signal.

wrong_answer_feedback.option: Delete all rows containing any missing Creatinine values
wrong_answer_feedback.feedback: Dropping rows shrinks the dataset by 800 critical patient cases and introduces severe survival selection bias.

wrong_answer_feedback.option: Fill all missing Creatinine values with 0.0
wrong_answer_feedback.feedback: Zero creatinine is physiologically impossible in living humans and corrupts downstream regression weights.

logs.message: IMPUTE_AGENT: Scanning dataset for missing values (total rows: 10,000)...
MISSINGNESS_TEST: Little's MCAR test p-value < 0.001 (Data is MAR). High correlation with BUN (r=0.78).
IMPUTE_AGENT: Ran 5 MICE iterations. Imputed 800 missing Creatinine values while preserving standard deviation.

day_title: Day 02: Schema Drift Detection & Type Coercion Guardrails
chapter_title: Schema Drift Detection & Type Coercion Guardrails

critical_concepts.definition: Enforcing strict field types, nullable constraints, and enum boundaries on incoming JSON/Parquet batches before pipeline ingestion.
critical_concepts.elaboration: Agents intercept upstream API payload shifts (e.g., zip codes changing from integers to strings, or new unmapped categorical levels) and apply safe type coercions or quarantine invalid rows.
critical_concepts.industry_application: Prevents silent downstream ML pipeline crashes and invalid ETL database corruption.

theory_content.title: Autonomous Data Quality Contracts & Schema Drift Governance
theory_content.content: Upstream microservices frequently change payload formats without notifying downstream analytics teams. An Agentic Data Preprocessing Specialist enforces strict schema contracts (Pydantic/Zod/Great Expectations), detects drift, and quarantines anomalous batches automatically.
theory_content.practical_takeaway: Never allow unvalidated raw JSON to hit downstream analytics tables without schema contract validation.
theory_content.analogy: Like an automated customs border checkpoint that checks passport formats and stamps before letting cargo enter the country.
theory_content.industry_case_study: When an international airline upstream ticketing service changed flight confirmation codes from alphanumeric strings to integers, downstream analytics pipelines crashed for 14 hours until automated schema contracts were introduced.

interactive_questions.title: Resolve Upstream Integer to String Schema Drift on Postal Codes
interactive_questions.prompt: An upstream checkout API updated its payload: `postal_code` changed from integer `90210` to string `'90210-4412'` and Canadian codes `'M5V 2T6'`. The ingestion pipeline failed with a type coercion error.
interactive_questions.question: What is the correct autonomous schema guardrail fix to deploy?
options: Force cast all strings to integer, converting Canadian postal codes to `NULL`
Update the data contract schema to string type `VARCHAR(16)`, apply international regex normalization (`^[A-Z0-9 -]+$`), and quarantine only malformed records to a dead-letter queue
Delete the postal code column from all historical databases
Halt all corporate data processing until the upstream team rolls back their software release
interactive_questions.answer: Update the data contract schema to string type `VARCHAR(16)`, apply international regex normalization (`^[A-Z0-9 -]+$`), and quarantine only malformed records to a dead-letter queue
interactive_questions.explanation: Postal codes are categorical strings worldwide. Updating the contract schema to string with regex validation accommodates extended ZIP+4 and international postal codes without dropping valid customer data.

wrong_answer_feedback.option: Force cast all strings to integer, converting Canadian postal codes to `NULL`
wrong_answer_feedback.feedback: Casting alphanumeric postal codes to integer corrupts all non-US and hyphenated postal records.

wrong_answer_feedback.option: Delete the postal code column from all historical databases
wrong_answer_feedback.feedback: Deleting the column destroys geographic analytics and logistics routing.

logs.message: DRIFT_DETECTED: Field `postal_code` received string values ('M5V 2T6', '90210-4412') violating INT32 contract.
TYPE_EVOLUTION: Applied safe VARCHAR(16) coercion and regex normalization. 0 records lost.

day_title: Day 03: Multimodal Outlier Scrubbing via IQR & Isolation Forests
chapter_title: Multimodal Outlier Scrubbing via IQR & Isolation Forests
prerequisites: Statistical Outlier Detection (Z-Score, IQR, Isolation Forest)

critical_concepts.definition: Unsupervised tree-based algorithm that isolates anomalies by randomly partitioning feature space; outliers require fewer random splits to isolate.
critical_concepts.elaboration: Agents detect non-linear multivariate anomalies that univariate IQR or Z-score thresholds miss (e.g. an 8-year-old with a $500k mortgage).
critical_concepts.industry_application: Cleans sensor noise, sensor drift, and fraudulent loan applications before training predictive models.

theory_content.title: Multidimensional Outlier Detection & Robust Scrubbing
theory_content.content: Real-world datasets contain typographical errors, sensor glitches, and malicious data injections. An Agentic Data Preprocessing Specialist deploys robust statistical boundaries (Tukey IQR fences) and Isolation Forests to differentiate genuine extreme events from corrupt noise.
theory_content.practical_takeaway: Winsorize or cap extreme values rather than blindly deleting rows when sample size is limited.
theory_content.analogy: Like an automated quality scanner on an apple packing line that discards rotten or plastic imitation apples while keeping unusually large but healthy apples.
theory_content.industry_case_study: When an autonomous vehicle training pipeline failed to scrub corrupted LiDAR sensor reflections, self-driving models hallucinated phantom obstacles on sunny days. Isolation Forest preprocessing eliminated 99.8% of sensor noise artifacts.

interactive_questions.title: Detect Multivariate Anomaly in Financial Credit Application Dataset
interactive_questions.prompt: An applicant has Income = $35,000 (normal range) and Credit Line = $100,000 (normal range). Univariate Z-scores are < 2.0 on both columns. However, Isolation Forest flags the row as an anomaly score of 0.89.
interactive_questions.question: Why did Isolation Forest flag this row when univariate tests failed, and what is the proper preprocessing action?
options: Isolation Forest is malfunctioning and should be disabled
The combination of low income with high credit line is a rare multivariate anomaly. The agent should flag this row for manual underwriting review or apply robust scaling
Multiply the applicant's income by 10 to make it match the credit line
Delete both income and credit line columns from the dataset
interactive_questions.answer: The combination of low income with high credit line is a rare multivariate anomaly. The agent should flag this row for manual underwriting review or apply robust scaling
interactive_questions.explanation: Multivariate anomalies occur when individual features look normal in isolation, but their joint co-occurrence is statistically improbable. Isolation Forest detects this high-dimensional interaction.

wrong_answer_feedback.option: Multiply the applicant's income by 10 to make it match the credit line
wrong_answer_feedback.feedback: Fabricating applicant data is fraud and destroys training integrity.

wrong_answer_feedback.option: Delete both income and credit line columns from the dataset
wrong_answer_feedback.feedback: Deleting primary financial features renders the credit scoring model useless.

logs.message: ANOMALY_ISOLATION: 42 records flagged with anomaly score > 0.85 (Multi-feature mismatch).
QUARANTINE_QUEUE: Routed 42 anomalous rows to underwriting audit partition.

day_title: Day 04: High-Cardinality Target Encoding & Leakage Prevention

critical_concepts.definition: Encoding high-cardinality categorical levels with the mean of the target variable computed strictly on out-of-fold training partitions with empirical Bayes smoothing.
critical_concepts.elaboration: Agents compute target encodings inside cross-validation splits to prevent target information from leaking from validation/test sets into training features.
critical_concepts.industry_application: Boosts GBDT (LightGBM/XGBoost/CatBoost) accuracy on features with 50,000+ categories (e.g. zip codes, merchant IDs) without overfitting.

theory_content.title: Preventing Catastrophic Data Leakage in Feature Engineering
theory_content.content: Target encoding categorical features with thousands of levels creates massive risk of data leakage and severe overfitting if calculated across the entire dataset. An Agentic Data Preprocessing Specialist enforces strict Out-of-Fold partitioning with m-estimate smoothing.
theory_content.practical_takeaway: Never fit encoders or scalers on the entire dataset; fit exclusively on training folds and transform test folds.
theory_content.analogy: Like a teacher who accidentally puts the final exam answer key in the study guide before the test, causing students to get 100% in practice but fail the actual test.
theory_content.industry_case_study: In a Kaggle fraud detection competition, multiple top teams scored 0.99 AUC in local validation but collapsed to 0.60 on the private leaderboard because they calculated target encodings before splitting training folds.

interactive_questions.title: Remediate Target Encoding Data Leakage on Merchant ID Feature
interactive_questions.prompt: A junior data scientist calculated target encoding for `merchant_id` (40,000 unique values) across all 1,000,000 rows prior to train/test split. Training AUC was 0.99, but Test AUC crashed to 0.58.
interactive_questions.question: What exact pipeline architecture fix must the Agentic Preprocessing Specialist execute?
options: One-hot encode all 40,000 merchant IDs into 40,000 sparse columns
Re-engineer the pipeline to perform K-Fold Out-of-Fold (OOF) target encoding with m-estimate smoothing strictly within the training set, mapping unseen merchant IDs to the global prior
Train the model for 10,000 more epochs to fix the test score
Remove the test set and only report the 0.99 training score
interactive_questions.answer: Re-engineer the pipeline to perform K-Fold Out-of-Fold (OOF) target encoding with m-estimate smoothing strictly within the training set, mapping unseen merchant IDs to the global prior
interactive_questions.explanation: Calculating target means across the entire dataset leaked target labels directly into feature values. Implementing K-Fold Out-of-Fold encoding with smoothing eliminates leakage and restores real test generalization.

wrong_answer_feedback.option: One-hot encode all 40,000 merchant IDs into 40,000 sparse columns
wrong_answer_feedback.feedback: One-hot encoding 40k categories creates massive sparse dimensionality, causing tree models to split inefficiently.

wrong_answer_feedback.option: Train the model for 10,000 more epochs to fix the test score
wrong_answer_feedback.feedback: More epochs on leaked features will only amplify overfitting.

logs.message: LEAKAGE_AUDITOR: Detected target correlation with feature `merchant_id_encoded` before K-Fold split.
OVERFIT_FLAG: Train AUC (0.99) vs Val AUC (0.58) shows 41% generalization gap.
OOF_ENCODER: Refactored to 5-Fold OOF Target Encoder with smoothing m=10.0. Val AUC restored to 0.884.

expectedToolCalls.purpose: Prevent target leakage during feature encoding

day_title: Day 05: Polars & Apache Arrow Memory DAG Pipeline Tuning
chapter_title: Polars & Apache Arrow Memory DAG Pipeline Tuning

critical_concepts.concept: Zero-Copy Arrow Memory Layout & Lazy Execution
critical_concepts.definition: Leveraging columnar memory buffers (Apache Arrow) and lazy Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) query optimization in Polars to execute transformations without intermediate memory allocations.
critical_concepts.elaboration: Agents optimize pipeline DAGs by pushing predicates (filters) and projections down to the scan layer, eliminating OOM errors on 100GB+ datasets.
critical_concepts.industry_application: Cuts cloud data warehouse compute costs by 80% and accelerates data ingestion pipelines from hours to minutes.

theory_content.title: High-Performance Zero-Copy Columnar Preprocessing Pipelines
theory_content.content: Pandas creates multiple redundant in-memory data copies, crashing on datasets exceeding available RAM. An Agentic Data Preprocessing Specialist architects streaming DAG pipelines using Polars and Apache Arrow with lazy predicate pushdown and chunked memory processing.
theory_content.practical_takeaway: Always write lazy query expressions (`pl.scan_parquet()`) so the optimizer can fuse filters and eliminate unnecessary column reads.
theory_content.analogy: Like planning your grocery store route before you enter the store so you pick up all items in one single lap without walking back and forth 20 times.
theory_content.industry_case_study: By migrating a financial tick data pipeline from Pandas to Polars with Arrow streaming, a quantitative fund reduced memory consumption from 128GB to 8GB and reduced daily batch processing runtime from 3.5 hours to 11 minutes.

interactive_questions.title: Optimize Out-of-Memory (OOM) Crash on 50GB Parquet Transformation
interactive_questions.prompt: An ETL job crashes with Out-Of-Memory on an 8GB RAM worker when loading a 50GB Parquet dataset using eager `pandas.read_parquet()` followed by `df[df['country'] == 'US']`.
interactive_questions.question: What Polars transformation pipeline should the agent deploy to process the data without OOM?
options: Rent a $5,000/month 1TB RAM cloud server and continue using eager pandas

Switch to Polars LazyFrame with `pl.scan_parquet()`, filter `country == 'US'` (predicate pushdown), select only required columns (projection pushdown), and collect via streaming engine `df.collect(streaming=True)`
Convert the Parquet files into 50,000 uncompressed CSV files
Sample only the first 100 rows and discard the rest of the 50GB dataset
interactive_questions.answer: Switch to Polars LazyFrame with `pl.scan_parquet()`, filter `country == 'US'` (predicate pushdown), select only required columns (projection pushdown), and collect via streaming engine `df.collect(streaming=True)`
interactive_questions.explanation: Lazy query optimization pushes filters down to the Parquet reader level, scanning only matching row groups and columns in streaming memory chunks, reducing memory footprint from 50GB to under 500MB.

wrong_answer_feedback.option: Rent a $5,000/month 1TB RAM cloud server and continue using eager pandas
wrong_answer_feedback.feedback: Throwing expensive cloud RAM at unoptimized code wastes budget and does not solve O(N) memory copy scaling issues.

wrong_answer_feedback.option: Convert the Parquet files into 50,000 uncompressed CSV files
wrong_answer_feedback.feedback: CSV is uncompressed and row-based, which multiplies disk I/O and makes memory consumption much worse.
